newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat firms on higher EU export rebate.
newsitem.headline: French wheat firms on higher EU export rebate.

text.p: French wheat prices firmed on Thursday after the European Union increased the rebate offered on soft wheat exports, dealers said.
The EU granted 311,3000 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a 16.59 Ecus rebate. Last week it awarded a rebate of 15.97 Ecus per tonne.
"All (wheat) positions gained five francs," one dealer said, adding the EU had raised its rebate despite firmer U.S markets.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 860 francs per tonne on November delivery, 855 francs on December delivery and 830 francs on January-March delivery.
"It is better than usual," another dealer said.
He estimated that a refund of 15.50 Ecus per tonne would have valued French wheat at around the level fetched by U.S. wheat prices.
The European Union had until now carefully avoided undercutting U.S. prices for fear of starting a subsidy war.
Wheat futures were sharply higher on MATIF, with the February 1997 expiry closing at 878 francs per tonne, up 13 francs on Wednesday.
Total volume was 267 lots, with 182 lots on the February contract alone.
